_meta.anti_fabrication_note: Lowe 1997 authentication hierarchy paper. The NSL fix (paper_001b) is the secure variant of NSPK. This record covers the Lowe hierarchy framework and its application to classify protocol security levels. Equations from NSL are already in paper_001b; this record documents the framework paper.
_meta.primary_source: Lowe, G. A Hierarchy of Authentication Specifications. Proc. 10th IEEE CSFW, pp.31-43, 1997. DOI:10.1109/CSFW.1997.596782

equation_source_page: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — NSL used as worked example; confirm pages in proceedings
attack_source_page: N/A — paper defines hierarchy, attacks used as classification examples
protocol_variant: NSL analysed under Lowe authentication hierarchy
cryptographic_parameters: Same as NSPK/NSL. Ka, Kb = public keys. Na, Nb = nonces.
original_equations:
A → B : {Na, A}Kb
B → A : {Na, Nb, B}Ka
A → B : {Nb}Kb

normalized_equations.description: B's identity included — Lowe's fix. Prevents MITM.

attacker_identity: N/A — protocol is secure under this hierarchy
security_violation: None. NSL achieves non-injective agreement (Lowe's hierarchy level 3) for both initiator and responder. The hierarchy paper proves: NSL satisfies aliveness, weak agreement, and non-injective agreement. Injective agreement also holds since each nonce is fresh.
verified_by: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — confirm exact page numbers and NSL equation notation against original IEEE CSFW 1997 proceedings
notes: This paper defines the 4-level authentication hierarchy: Aliveness < Weak Agreement < Non-Injective Agreement < Injective Agreement. NSL achieves all four. The original NSPK (paper_001) fails Non-Injective Agreement at the responder. This paper is primarily a framework contribution; NSL is used as a worked example. Paired with paper_001 (NSPK attack) and paper_001b (NSL secure) for ML training contrast.
